newsitem.title: INDIA: India RBI buys spot dollars as rupee stays buoyant.
newsitem.headline: India RBI buys spot dollars as rupee stays buoyant.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) bought spot dollars on Tuesday afternoon as the rupee continued to be buoyant, dealers said.
"They bought at 35.74," said a foreign bank dealer.
Some banks said RBI checked with them but did not buy. "They came off and on asking for prices off and on," said a dealer.
RBI aggressively intervened in the forward section on Monday and many banks were expecting it to resume buying forward dollars on Tuesday.
But RBI surprised the market again by shifting to spot.
RBI's purchases did not impact the exchange rate. Spot dollar was quoted at 35.732/737 in latest trades, little changed from the opening level of 35.73/74, dealers said.
Premiums on far-forward maturities edged down in afternoon trade, but premiums on near term maturities were largely steady.
